assign.request: N even columns computed from the room, fixed navigation, and pages that slide. The owner: 'I want to focus on N even columns. I think it was a mistake to use different sized columns, at least initially. The N should be computed on window resize to compute based on the columns min/max or recommended width, and available screen (or container?) space. For example, if we have 3k pixels, and each column wants to be 1000 px, then we can render 3 of them. Instead of continuous Miller columns, we want fixed (non janky) navigation. In order to avoid jumps, we could try to animate the pages sliding left/right? Look into how to animate pages.'

assign.now: the mode is in core and the Finder wears it - measuring nav stability and the slide

log.msg: SPELLING: this.columns({ even: true }), not a declared columns: "even". A page config is Object.assign-ed OVER the prototype, so columns: as DATA would shadow the columns() METHOD and the next page writing initialize(){ this.columns(); } dies on "this.columns is not a function" - the documented opens() collision. The option is stored as the prefixed field column_even for the same reason.

MEASURING TRICK: --page-column-max: var(--page-column-even-w) with NO fallback. Unset, the declaration is invalid at computed-value time and the base rule max-width falls back to the recommendation - so even_columns() reads the recommendation in px off getComputedStyle(body).maxWidth and the browser resolves the em and the cqi. One number, one place, no second copy in JS.

N for the Finder, default recommendation: 400 -> phone regime untouched (flex 1 0 100%); 1280 -> N=1, 1051px (recommended 601.6); 1920 -> N=2, 838.5px (rec 704.3); 3440 -> N=3, 1055.3px (rec 828). The em ramps with --size (15.04/16/18px), which is why 3440 gives 3 and not 4.

NAV STABILITY, Finder, open a child and re-measure every column already open: width 0 and nav-link y 0 at ALL FOUR widths, every click. x inside the row 0 too. x on screen is 0 until the row is full (at 3440 the 2nd and 3rd column open with nothing moving at all) and then exactly ONE column width - that move is the slide, never a fraction of a column.

BLOCKED briefly: public/framework/ui/decision/decision.js (another agent, outside my fence) has an unclosed css(backtick) template - SyntaxError "Invalid left-hand side expression in postfix operation" - which takes EVERY page on the site down. Found by node --check over the 38 files modified in the last 40 minutes. Not mine to fix; measuring resumes when it clears.

assign.now: the slide is measured and shipped - writing the docs

log.msg: SLIDE, measured headless, 5 runs x 2 widths, frames over 50ms during the move: native smooth scroll 0 long frames (worst frame 16.8ms) | FLIP, translateX + Web Animations 0 (16.8ms) | View Transitions 23 (worst 116.7ms, all at 3440, and it drops ~20 of the ~56 frames in the window) | instant, today 0. Smooth scroll and FLIP tie on jank, so the cheaper one wins: the row ALREADY scrolls, so asking the browser to animate it costs one word.

SLIDE SHIPPED as scroll_column(slide) + column_slide(), NOT as scroll-behavior: smooth in the sheet - the sheet cannot tell an arrival from a click. Verified: a cold load straight at a 4-deep url polls ONE distinct scrollLeft (3153 at 1280, 1055 at 3440) = the arrival is instant; a click ramps through 38 values over 600ms at 1280 and 33 over 517ms at 3440, 0 long frames; prefers-reduced-motion: reduce gives 2 values and 0ms.

LAB, three rows, the pages own readout against an independent headless measurement of the same click, at 400/1280/1920/3440: today 129px nav / 225px widths at all three desktop widths | stable 0/0 | even 0/0 and N = 3 (351px each). They agree exactly at every width. At 400 all three read 0/0 and the even row shows no N: the phone regime is untouched and even_columns() returns null under 32em of row.

/imagine/ WOULD-BE numbers (measured by applying the class and the arithmetic in the browser, nothing edited): 1280 -> N=2, 640px each, rail 205 -> 640 | 1920 -> N=2, 960px each, rail 307 -> 960 | 3440 -> N=4, 860px each, rail 432 -> 860. It has 25 rail children, of which 6/9/3 already sit below the fold at 1280/1920/3440 and the even mode does not change that. The real cost is horizontal: with N=2 the rail leaves the screen the moment you are two columns deep, taking all 25 with it.

THE THREE EXEMPTIONS VERIFIED, not just documented. full at 3440: one visible column at 3166px, the whole row, crumbs intact. The drag at 1920: 839 -> 539 (the 300px move exactly), double-click -> 839, the even width back. The 400 phone regime: flex reads 1 0 100%, unchanged, and even_columns() returns null there.

CRAWL: 14 pages x 4 widths (400/1280/1920/3440) - the Finder and its Words column, the demo box, all four uses/*, both doc pages, core/Page, the lab, /imagine/, /framework/, /. Zero console errors, zero .md-error, zero horizontal overflow. The pages that did NOT switch measure the same as before the change (uses/docs 704px, workbench 268px).

LEFT OPEN, deliberately: (1) floor vs round - floor never goes below the recommendation but leaves up to recommended-1 px of slack per column (1055 against 828 at 3440, ~227px of each column is padding past the prose measure); round fills tighter and can go under. The owners sentence asked for floor. (2) /imagine/ did not switch - its rail is its root, and N=2 at 1280/1920 takes all 25 entries off screen two columns deep. Numbers are in the doc as the next step. (3) Only the even mode slides; dropping this.column_even && from column_slide() makes it universal.

assign.outcome:
**`this.columns({ even: true })` landed in core** - every open column the same width, N computed from the room, and a row that slides by exactly one column instead of jumping. Additive: the four `uses/*` screens, the demo box and `/imagine/` are untouched, so the two behaviours are one click apart.

![the lab's third row at 1920](/framework/ai/2026-09-17/even-columns/even-row-1920.png)

**N, the Finder, on the default recommendation** - `N = max(1, floor(row / recommended))`, `width = row / N`, measured on the row (not the window) by a `ResizeObserver`:

| screen | row | recommended | N | each |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | 400 | - | - | the `< 32em` phone regime, untouched |
| 1280 | 1051 | 601.6 | **1** | 1051px |
| 1920 | 1677 | 704.3 | **2** | 838.5px |
| 3440 | 3166 | 828 | **3** | 1055.3px |

**Fixed navigation: 0 and 0.** Open a child and re-measure every column already open - **0px of width change, 0px of nav-link movement, at all four widths**, and a column's x *inside the row* never changes either. Nothing moves on screen at all until the row is full; at 3440 two more columns open with zero movement. The lab prints the same numbers from inside the page and an independent headless measurement agrees exactly: today **129 / 225**, the proposal **0 / 0**, even **0 / 0** with **N = 3 (351px each)**.

**The slide: native smooth scroll**, on frames over 50ms during the move (5 runs x 2 widths) - smooth scroll **0** (worst frame 16.8ms) - FLIP **0** (16.8ms) - View Transitions **23** (116.7ms). The first two tie, so the cheaper wins: the row is already a scroller. It is an argument, not `scroll-behavior` in the sheet, because a sheet cannot tell an arrival from a click - verified, a four-deep cold load polls one distinct `scrollLeft`, a click ramps through 38 over 600ms, reduced motion gives 0ms.

**Three things still beat the mode, each on purpose and each verified:** `full` (it claims the host - 3166px of 3166 at 3440), a drag (839 -> 539 -> 839 on a double-click), and the phone regime.
